faq: What if you cannot fix a bug?
We tell you clearly why, for example when the fault sits inside a platform feature or a closed app. We then suggest a workaround or contact the app maker with the details.
Do I have to describe every bug perfectly?
No. A screenshot or a short screen recording and the page link is enough. We reproduce the problem ourselves and ask questions if something is unclear.
Can you fix a bug in a paid app?
We fix how the app is set up and how it sits in your theme. If the code inside the app is at fault, we report it to the maker with evidence.
Do you work on live stores?
Yes, carefully. We keep a backup of what we change and make risky edits on a test copy, so shoppers do not see half-finished work.

desc:
Ecommerce bug fixes for stores means finding why a page, button or checkout step stopped working and repairing it in your own theme or settings. Ecom Swift LLC reproduces each problem, fixes it and tests it on the devices where it failed.

## What counts as a store bug?

A store bug is any behavior that differs from what you and your shoppers expect. Examples include an add to cart button that does nothing, a discount code that will not apply, a menu that will not open on a phone, an image that overlaps text or a contact form that never sends. Some bugs are loud and obvious. Others only appear in one browser or on one product, which is why they can go unnoticed for weeks.

## Why unfixed bugs cost more than they seem

A shopper who meets a broken page rarely reports it. They leave. If the broken part is the cart or checkout, the loss is a sale that was already decided. If it is a form, you lose an enquiry you never knew existed.

Bugs also tend to spread. A quick patch placed on top of an earlier patch can interact in strange ways, and each new problem is harder to trace. Fixing the cause early keeps the theme tidy and cheaper to maintain.

## How repairs improve the store

The benefit of a fix is mostly the removal of friction. A working button, a clear error message and a layout that reads well on a small screen all help a visitor move forward. Fewer failed actions mean fewer abandoned carts that were avoidable.

There is a quieter benefit as well. When we explain what caused each bug, you learn which kinds of change put the store at risk, such as installing an app, pasting code or editing a template. That knowledge makes future work safer.

## What a proper bug fix includes

- A written description of each problem, with the steps that trigger it.
- Reproduction on the same device and browser where you saw it.
- A check of the browser console for script errors.
- Review of the theme code, settings and apps involved.
- A fix made in your theme or configuration, not a workaround that hides the symptom.
- Testing on phone and desktop after the repair.
- A cross-browser check on the main browsers.
- A look at neighboring pages that share the same code.
- A short note on the cause of each bug.
- Screenshots that show the before and after.

## What we do

You send a list of the problems you have seen, in whatever words come naturally. Screenshots and screen recordings help, but they are not required. We work through the list, reproduce each issue and trace it to its source. Common sources are a theme template, a conflict between two apps, a stale script or a setting that changed.

We repair the cause inside your store, usually in a copy of the theme first when the platform allows it, and then on the live store. Basic handles a few bugs with notes. Standard adds a sweep of the home, product, cart and checkout pages to catch problems you have not spotted. Premium covers a larger set, clears code errors in the theme, resolves app conflicts and gives you a prevention checklist for future changes. If a fault belongs to a paid app or to your platform, we tell you plainly and explain what the vendor must do.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Note the device, browser and page where each problem appears.
- Send screenshots or a short screen recording when you can.
- List the bugs in order of how much they hurt sales.
- Tell us about any change you made just before the problem began.
- Test your own store on a phone every time you edit it.

**Avoid:**
- Pasting snippets from forums into your theme without a backup.
- Installing a second app to fix a problem caused by the first.
- Editing the live theme directly when a copy is available.
- Hiding an error message instead of solving its cause.
- Assuming a bug is fixed because it works on your own computer.

## Who this is for

This suits an owner whose store started behaving oddly after an update, an app install or a theme edit. It suits a seller who gets occasional customer messages about something not working but cannot reproduce it. It also suits a team that has a growing list of small annoyances and no developer on staff.

## What we need from you

Send the list of problems and the address of the store. We need access as a collaborator, staff or developer user, and we ask for no passwords. If a bug only appears at checkout, tell us which payment method and device you used so we can follow the same path.
